note: The script is artificial and recalls ms. St. Petersburg n.s. syr. 11, of possible Sinaitic provenance

para.as_written: ܫܠܡ ܟܬܒܐ ܗܢܐ ܕܐܝܬܘܗܝ ܦܘܪܫ ܩܪܝܢܐ / ܘܩܪ̈ܝܬܐ ܕܟܠܗ ܫܢܬܐ ܐܝܟ ܛܟܣܐ ܕܥܕܬܐ / ܩܕܝܫܬܐ ܫܘܒܚܐ ܠܗ ܠܐܠܗܐ ܕܥܠ ܫܡܗ / [ܡ‍]‍ܫܪܝܢܢ (؟) ܘܫܘܒܚܐ ܠܒܪܗ ܡܚܝܝܢܐ (sic !) ܕܗܘܝܘ / ܚܝܠ ܘܥܕܪ ܘܠܪܘܚܗ ܚܝܐ ܘܩܕܝܫܐ ܕܗܘܝܘ / ܫܡܠܝ ܘܫܠܡ ܐܝܟ ܨܒܝܢܗ ܕܠܗ / ܫܘܒܚܐ ܠܥܠܡ ܥܠܡܝܢ ܐܡܝܢ ܘܐܡܝܢ ܀ / ܐܣܬܝܟ ܕܝܢ ܟܬܒܐ ܗܢܐ ܕܟܠܗܝܢ ܩܪ̈ܝܬܐ / ܘܩܪ̈ܝܢܐ ܕܟܠܗ ܫܢܬܐ ܕܥܐܕ̈ܐ ܘܕܚܕ / ܒܫܒ̈ܐ ܕܪܡܫܐ ܘܕܟܢܫܐ ܐܝܟ ܕܛܟܣܐ / ܫܦܝܪܐ ܒܕܝܪܐ ܛܒܝܒܬܐ ܕܡܪܝ ܡܘܫܐ / ܪܝܫܐ ܕܢܒܝ̈ܐ ܛܘܪܐ ܩܕܝܫܐ ܕܣܝܢܝ. / ܟܘܠ ܕܩܪܐ ܒܗ ܐܘ ܢܣܚ ܡܢܗ ܢܨܠܐ // ܥܠ ܡܚܝܠܐ ܘܚܛܝܐ ܕܟܬܒ ܠܐܘܢ / ܩܫܝܫܐ ܡܣܟܢܐ ܟܕ ܠܐ ܫܐܘܐ (sic !) ܡܛܘܠ / ܐܠܗܐ ܕܢܬܚܢܢ ܒܝܘܡ ܕܝܢܐ ܘܢܫܟܚ / ܪ̈ܚܡܐ ܩܕܡ ܐܠܗܐ ܒܨܠܘܬܐ ܕܟܠܗܘܢ / ܩܕܝ̈ܫܐ ܕܪ̈ܥܝܘ ܠܐܠܗܐ. ܘܒܨܠܘ̈ܬܐ / ܕܝܠܕܬ ܐܠܗܐ ܡܪܬܝ ܡܪܝܡ ܘܗܫܐ / ܘܒܟܠܙܒܢ ܘܠܥܠܡ ܥܠܡܝܢ ܐܡܝܢ܀ / ܘܗ̇ܘ ܕܩܪܐ ܠܐ ܢܥܕܘܠ ܕܠܐ ܢܡܘܬ ܐܢ / ܐܫܟܚ ܕܛܡܐ ܡܕܡ ܐܘܟܝܬ ܦܘܕܐ / ܐܢܐ ܓܝܪ ܐܝܟ ܡܚܝܠܘܬܝ ܟܬܒܬ ܡܕܡ / ܕܐܫܟܚܬܐ (sic !) ܘܗܐ ܝܬܘܗܝ (sic !) ܟܬܒܐ ܗܢܐ / ܬܪ̈ܝܢ ܟܬܒܐ ܡܛܠ ܕܠܐ ܐܫܟܚܝܬܝ (sic !) ܐܥܒܕܝܘܗܝ (sic !) / ܚܕܝ (sic !) ܀ ܫܠܡܬ ܟܬܒܐ ܗܢܐ ܫܢܬ ܀ / ܐܠܦ ܪ̄ ܡ̄ ܕ̄ ܕܐܠܟܣܢܕܪܘܣ ܒܪ / ܦܝܠܝܦܘܣ ܡܩܕܘܢܝܐ: ܘܒܛܝܝܐ / [a line left blank] / ܒܝܪܚ ܐܝܠܘܠ ܝ̄ ܕ̄ ܒܗ ܝܘܡ ܫܒܬܐ / ܝܘܡ ܥܐܕܐ ܩܕܝܫܐ ܕܪܘܡܪܡܝܗܝ / ܕܨܠܝܒܐ ܡܝܩܪܐ
translation: Completed is this book, which is the lectionary (lit. ‘separate readings and recitations’) for the entire year according to the order of the Holy Church. Glory to God in whose name we begin, and glory to His life-giving Son who strengthened and assisted, and to His living and holy Spirit who fulfilled and completed according to His will, to whom be glory forever and ever, amen and amen. / This book of all readings and recitations for the entire year, feasts and Sundays’ vespers and Eucharists, has been completed; (which is) according to the beautiful order in the blessed monastery of Saint Moses, chief of the prophets, the holy Mount Sinai. Everyone who reads it or copies from it, pray for the weak and sinful one who wrote it, Leo, the poor priest, although he is unworthy, so that for God’s sake he may find mercy on the day of judgment and find compassion before God through the prayer of all the saints who pleased God, and through the prayers of the Mother of God, my Lady Mary, now and always and forever and ever, amen. / And whoever reads (from it), do not criticize lest he dies, if he finds something corrupt or a mistake, for I have written according to my weakness what I found; and behold, this book (consists of) two parts, because I could not make it single. This book was completed in the year 1244 of Alexander, the son of Philip the Macedonian and of the Arabic [a line left blank]. In the month of Elul (August), on the 14th day, on Saturday, the holy feast day of the Exaltation of the venerable Cross.

note.value: Foliation in pencil in upper or lower margin, which sometimes includes numbered folios with the suffix a or b (e.g., f. 63, followed by f. 63a and f. 63b)
The original first five folios of the codex are fragmentary, not numbered, and are not considered here; the sixth folio in the codex is numbered 1, followed here
Foliation in Syriac letters in the top margin of each recto side added by a later hand. The actual sequence suggests that one folio preceding f. 1 is missing.
No visible quire signatures. The quire composition cannot be determined from the images. Nonetheless, the manuscript appears complete, with only one folio missing.
Leather front and back covers; leather spine with reinforced fabric. Front cover detached; back cover attached; spine partially detached.
Many folios exhibit significant damage, occasionally leaving only a narrow strip of the inner margin intact.
Until ca. f. 32, spine slants outward, resulting in curled folios

Judging from the indications of the scribe (f. 88r–v, 110r), the actual lectionary is the second (companion) volume of the original set of two. The first volume, covering the readings for the feasts, has not survived.
Palimpsest throughout with underwriting in CPA, Syriac and Armenian
